ei.title: Why Water Bodies Do Not Mix
ei.subject: 11월_2022 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Why Water Bodies Do Not Mix

fullPassage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are essentially two glasses of water but with a completely different chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and heat it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would remain separate because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The warmer water would float on the surface of the cold water because of its lighter weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that differ in temperature and salt content; for this reason, they do not mix.

questions.passage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are (A)[partially / essentially] two glasses of water but with a completely different chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and heat it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would remain (B)[separate / mixed] because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The warmer water would (C)[float / sink] on the surface of the cold water because of its lighter weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that differ in temperature and salt content; for this reason, they do not mix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 두 물은 '본질적으로(essentially)' 같은 물이지만 화학적 조성이 달라 '분리된(separate)' 상태로 남고, 따뜻한 물은 위로 '뜬다(float)'.
det.analysis:
(A) essentially(본질적으로): 원문 일치 — 사실상 같은 물이라는 흐름
(B) separate(분리된): 원문 일치 — 조성이 달라 섞이지 않고 분리됨
(C) float(뜨다): 원문 일치 — 따뜻한 물이 표면에 뜬다
② partially(부분적으로) ③ mixed(섞인) ④ sink(가라앉다)는 모두 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are essentially two glasses of water but with a completely different chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and (A)[freeze / heat] it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would remain separate because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The (B)[warmer / cooler] water would float on the surface of the cold water because of its (C)[lighter / heavier] weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that differ in temperature and salt content; for this reason, they do not mix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 한 잔을 '데우면(heat)' 온도차가 생기고, '더 따뜻한(warmer)' 물은 '더 가벼운(lighter)' 무게 때문에 위로 뜬다.
det.analysis:
(A) heat(데우다): 원문 일치 — 오렌지주스 잔을 데움
(B) warmer(더 따뜻한): 원문 일치 — 더 따뜻한 물이 위로 뜸
(C) lighter(더 가벼운): 원문 일치 — 가벼운 무게 때문에 표면에 뜸
① freeze(얼리다) ③ cooler(더 시원한) ④ heavier(더 무거운)는 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are essentially two glasses of water but with a completely different chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and heat it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would (A)[stop / remain] separate because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The warmer water would float on the (B)[surface / bottom] of the cold water because of its lighter weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that (C)[differ / match] in temperature and salt content; for this reason, they do not mix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 두 물은 섞이지 않고 '남으며(remain)', 따뜻한 물은 찬 물의 '표면(surface)'에 뜨고, 바다 물은 온도·염분이 '다르다(differ)'.
det.analysis:
(A) remain(남다): 원문 일치 — 분리된 채로 남음
(B) surface(표면): 원문 일치 — 찬 물의 표면에 뜸
(C) differ(다르다): 원문 일치 — 온도·염분이 다름
① stop(멈추다) ② bottom(바닥) ④ match(일치하다)는 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are essentially two glasses of water but with a completely ①<u>different</u> chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and heat it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would remain ②<u>separate</u> because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The warmer water would ③<u>float</u> on the surface of the cold water because of its lighter weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that ④<u>match</u> in temperature and salt content; for this reason, they do not mix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ match(일치하다)는 부적절. 바다의 물은 온도와 염분이 서로 '다르기(differ)' 때문에 섞이지 않는다는 흐름.
det.analysis:
① different(다른): 원문 그대로 — 적절
② separate(분리된): 원문 그대로 — 적절
③ float(뜨다): 원문 그대로 — 적절
④ match(일치하다) ←정답: 원문은 differ(다르다). 물이 '일치하면' 섞이지 않는다는 이유가 성립하지 않음

det.korean: ① same(같은)은 부적절. 주스를 섞은 두 잔은 완전히 '다른(different)' 화학적 조성을 갖는다는 흐름.
det.analysis:
① same(같은) ←정답: 원문은 different(다른). '완전히 같은 조성'이면 뒤의 분리 설명이 성립하지 않음
② separate(분리된): 원문 그대로 — 적절
③ warmer(더 따뜻한): 원문 그대로 — 적절
④ lighter(더 가벼운): 원문 그대로 — 적절

det.korean: ② mixed(섞인)는 부적절. 두 물은 조성과 온도가 달라 '분리된(separate)' 채로 남는다는 흐름.

② mixed(섞인) ←정답: 원문은 separate(분리된). 뒤에 '섞이지 않는다'가 이어지므로 '섞인 채로 남는다'는 모순
③ warmer(더 따뜻한): 원문 그대로 — 적절

questions.passage: Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would remain separate because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The __________ (warm) water would float on the surface of the cold water because of its lighter weight.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 뒤의 the cold water(찬 물)와 비교하는 문맥이므로 비교급 warmer로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: the ___ water가 the cold water와 대조되어 '더 따뜻한 물'을 의미 → 비교급 warmer

questions.passage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are essentially two glasses of water but with a completely different chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and heat it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they __________; however, they would remain separate because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The warmer water would float on the surface of the cold water because of its lighter weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that differ in temperature and salt content; for this reason, they do not mix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: met(만났다). 두 물이 서로 맞닿아 '만나는' 경계에서만 조금 섞인다는 흐름.
det.analysis:
① met(만났다) ←정답: 'where they ___'로 두 물이 접촉하는 지점
② grew(자랐다): 문맥 부적합
③ stopped(멈췄다): 문맥 부적합
④ cooked(요리했다): 문맥 부적합
det.tip: where they met = 그들이 만난 곳(경계)

questions.passage: Take two glasses of water. Put a little bit of orange juice into one and a little bit of lemon juice into the other. What you have are essentially two glasses of water but with a completely different chemical makeup. If we take the glass containing orange juice and heat it, we will still have two different glasses of water with different chemical makeups, but now they will also have different temperatures. If we could magically remove the glasses, we would find the two water bodies would not mix well. Perhaps they would mix a little where they met; however, they would remain separate because of their different chemical makeups and temperatures. The warmer water would float on the surface of the cold water because of its lighter weight. In the ocean we have bodies of water that differ in temperature and __________; for this reason, they do not mix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: salt content(염분 함량). 바다의 물덩어리는 온도와 '염분 함량'이 달라 섞이지 않는다.
det.analysis:
① air pressure(기압): 물덩어리가 섞이지 않는 이유와 무관
② salt content(염분 함량) ←정답: 'differ in temperature and ___'로 온도와 함께 나열되는 요소
③ water depth(수심): 문맥 부적합
④ sun light(햇빛): 문맥 부적합
det.tip: differ in temperature and salt content = 온도와 염분 함량이 다르다
